title: Sheaf pullback and its scheme equality loci
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work on the big fppf site of $S$ [def-pc-fppf-site], with sheaves of sets as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and scheme representability as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $F,G,H$ be sheaves, let $f:F\to H$ and $g:G\to H$ be natural transformations, and suppose that $\Delta_F$ and $\Delta_G$ are representable by schemes. Define the presheaf $P$ by $P(T)=\{(x,y)\in F(T)\times G(T):f(x)=g(y)\}$ with componentwise restriction. Then $P$ is a sheaf. For every scheme $T$ over $S$ and sections $p_j=(x_j,y_j)\in P(T)$, $j=1,2$, let $A$ represent $h_T\times_{F\times F}F$ along $(x_1,x_2)$ and $\Delta_F$, and let $B$ represent $h_T\times_{G\times G}G$ along $(y_1,y_2)$ and $\Delta_G$. The scheme $A\times_TB$ [def-pc-fibre-product] represents $h_T\times_{P\times P}P$ along $(p_1,p_2)$ and $\Delta_P$, compatibly with the maps to $T$. In particular $\Delta_P$ is representable. For every sheaf $Q$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,P)\to\{(a,b)\in\operatorname{Hom}(Q,F)\times\operatorname{Hom}(Q,G):f\circ a=g\circ b\}$ given by the two projections is a bijection, with inverse sending $(a,b)$ to the natural transformation $q\mapsto(a(q),b(q))$.

proof.text: The compatible-pair cone [def-trf-sheaf-pullback-cone] is a limit: evaluation at each test scheme identifies it with Mathlib Types.pullbackLimitCone, and evaluation jointly reflects limits. Apply closure of the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] under limits (Mathlib CategoryTheory.Sites.Limits, ObjectProperty.prop_of_isLimit) to the cospan of F,G,H. This includes empty covering sieves.

proof.text: Use the limit universal property of the explicit compatible-pair cone [def-trf-sheaf-pullback-cone]. Send a map c to its two projections and send a compatible pair (a,b) to the pullback lift. The two projection identities and pullback hom_ext prove that these maps are inverse. Applying the lift projection identities at each test object and each section shows that the inverse has literal value (a(q),b(q)). Sheaf morphisms are presheaf morphisms because sheaves form a full subcategory [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 04T9 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal), proof, first two conditions; Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces), universal-property paragraph

proof.text: Apply Yoneda to the scheme pullback square [def-pc-fibre-product], giving a presheaf pullback W=h_(A times_T B) with maps rA,rB. Let r=rA;pA=rB;pB. Projecting the two given representing-square equations [def-trf-algebraic-space] onto each product factor shows r;a1 and r;a2 have identical F and G components. The compatible-pair pullback universal property therefore gives r;a1=r;a2. Thus q=r;a1 and r form a commuting square over the diagonal of P.

source.place: Tag 04T9 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces-over-sheaf-with-representable-diagonal), proof, first two conditions; Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces), universal-property paragraph

proof.text: For a cone (a:Z to P,b:Z to hT) over the P-diagonal square, projecting its equation gives a=b;a1=b;a2. Their F and G components give cones over the A and B representing squares [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Lift into hA and hB, then into W; its two composites are a and b. Uniqueness follows since pA and pB are monomorphisms, being base changes of diagonals, and rA is a base change of pB, hence r is mono. This proves the required IsPullback square. For an arbitrary test map alpha:hT to P times P take a1=alpha;prod.fst and a2=alpha;prod.snd. Use representability of the F and G diagonals to obtain A and B, apply the square just proved, and use prod.lift of these projections equals alpha. This proves representability of the diagonal of P.

lean.statement: theorem sheafPullback_diagonal {S : Scheme.{u}} (F G H : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (f : F.obj ⟶ H.obj) (g : G.obj ⟶ H.obj) (hF : IsRepresentable (prod.lift (𝟙 F.obj) (𝟙 F.obj))) (hG : IsRepresentable (prod.lift (𝟙 G.obj) (𝟙 G.obj))) : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt ∧ IsRepresentable (prod.lift (𝟙 (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt) (𝟙 (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt)) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a₁ a₂ : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt) (A B : Over S) (pA : A ⟶ T) (pB : B ⟶ T) (qA : yoneda.obj A ⟶ F.obj) (qB : yoneda.obj B ⟶ G.obj), IsPullback qA (yoneda.map pA) (prod.lift (𝟙 F.obj) (𝟙 F.obj)) (prod.lift (a₁ ≫ (sheafPullbackCone f g).fst) (a₂ ≫ (sheafPullbackCone f g).fst)) → IsPullback qB (yoneda.map pB) (prod.lift (𝟙 G.obj) (𝟙 G.obj)) (prod.lift (a₁ ≫ (sheafPullbackCone f g).snd) (a₂ ≫ (sheafPullbackCone f g).snd)) → ∃ q : yoneda.obj (Limits.pullback pA pB) ⟶ (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt, IsPullback q (yoneda.map (Limits.pullback.fst pA pB ≫ pA)) (prod.lift (𝟙 (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt) (𝟙 (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt)) (prod.lift a₁ a₂)) ∧ ∀ Q : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), ∃ e : (Q.obj ⟶ (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt) ≃ {ab : (Q.obj ⟶ F.obj) × (Q.obj ⟶ G.obj) // ab.1 ≫ f = ab.2 ≫ g}, (∀ c : Q.obj ⟶ (sheafPullbackCone f g).pt, (e c).val = (c ≫ (sheafPullbackCone f g).fst, c ≫ (sheafPullbackCone f g).snd)) ∧ ∀ (ab : {ab : (Q.obj ⟶ F.obj) × (Q.obj ⟶ G.obj) // ab.1 ≫ f = ab.2 ≫ g}) (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ) (q : Q.obj.obj T), ((e.symm ab).app T q).val = (ab.val.1.app T q, ab.val.2.app T q)
